<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916062_theRebbe_542" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916062_theRebbe_542__p006">
  <section v="15">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the connection of the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" to the redemption of Yud Tes Kislev, emphasizing that the revelation of Chassidus brings about a redemption characterized by peace, without war, through the level of Yechidah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And according to this, the connection of “He redeemed my soul in peace” etc. will also be understood</t>
    <t s="1">[that the emphasis here is that the redemption is specifically in peace]</t>
    <t s="2">to the redemption of Yud Tes Kislev</t>
    <t s="3">(the revelation of the teachings of Chassidus),</t>
    <t s="4">for it is explained in many places</t>
    <t s="5">that the essence of the teachings of Chassidus is the revelation of the inner dimension of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="6">the innermost aspect of wisdom, the innermost aspect of Abba</t>
    <t s="7">(which is the innermost aspect of Atik)</t>
    <t s="8">is the level of Yechidah,</t>
    <t s="9">and from the perspective of the level of Yechidah, even when there is a state of multiplicity,</t>
    <t s="10">the redemption is in peace</t>
    <t s="11">(and it can be said that this is even more than the concept of “He makes peace in His high places”</t>
    <t s="12">according to the explanation of the Maggid,</t>
    <t s="13">which is analogous to the utter nullification of the ministering angel when he comes before the king,</t>
    <t s="14">unlike here, where the wills are nullified from the outset),</t>
    <t s="15">that there is no need for war at all,</t>
    <t s="16">and on the contrary, the service is specifically through pleasant ways and ways of peace,</t>
    <t s="17">and through this it is brought about</t>
    <t s="18">(as he concludes in the aforementioned Igeres HaKodesh)</t>
    <t s="19">that it will be “as water reflects a face,”</t>
    <t s="20">that is, as the conclusion of the verse</t>
    <t s="21">“so is the heart of man to man,”</t>
    <t s="22">and the intention in this is also regarding the level of the Supernal Man,</t>
    <t s="23">that there will be the light</t>
    <t s="24">of the “face of the King of life,”</t>
    <t s="25">that from this there will be</t>
    <t s="26">(as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded</t>
    <t s="27">on the verse “He redeemed my soul in peace”)</t>
    <t s="28">“He redeemed me and my sons from among the nations,”</t>
    <t s="29">and this is that very soon “with me is the man, King Moshiach,”</t>
    <t s="30">through the service</t>
    <t s="31">of “your springs will burst forth”</t>
    <t s="32">outwardly,</t>
    <t s="33">which primarily began</t>
    <t s="34">after the redemption of Yud Tes Kislev,</t>
    <t s="35">that out of rest and joy and a good heart, and in a manner of peace, the departure from exile will be in peace, in the true and complete redemption, very soon, from He Who is Peace.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
